title: Second-hand smoke from neighbouring HDB flats and official health guidelines
asked: Mr Shawn Loh asked whether the Ministry of Health will study the negative health impact of sustained second-hand smoke from neighbouring HDB units, especially on children and the elderly, and whether it will issue official guidelines on that health impact to inform future policies on regulating smoking out of windows in HDB flats.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said the health harms of second-hand smoke are well established in scientific literature, linked to respiratory illness, cardiovascular diseases and cancers such as breast and lung cancer. She said the health effects of prolonged exposure were previously addressed in MOH's answer to oral Question No 12 on 2 October 2018, and that there are currently no plans to issue official guidelines on the negative health impact of second-hand smoke. MOH has worked with MSE and NEA, which have progressively prohibited smoking at more than 49,000 public places, including common corridors and void decks. In supplementary replies, she said MOH already takes the health impact into account when rolling out policies, and that translating and enforcing measures in spaces may not directly lie within MOH's remit.
